issues.claim: §4.11 *The clock* forbids the weeks that the history replay uses. (1) (l. 7700-7702) says the map's time is an integer week and 'a standalone map starts at week 0'. (3) (l. 7713) gives the week of the year as '(week mod 52) + 1'. V06 §3.20.2 (4) (l. 2882-2885) and V06 l. 836 date the replay's coarse epochs at signed weeks before the creation week, negative on a standalone map, and read the week of the year as 'the non-negative remainder of §4.11 The clock (3)'s formula'. The base admits no week before creation. Its formula is undefined for a negative week: a truncating mod gives a week of the year of 0 or below, which matches no CalendarRow season, so the Works' pauses and §8.2's season rows read nothing (silent wrong). V06 note 12 hands this to pipeline.
issues.required_change: *The clock* (1) adds: 'the history replay's coarse epochs (§4.11 *History-first generation*; V06 §3.20.2 (4)) carry signed weeks before the creation week, negative on a standalone map; no other event is dated before the creation week'. (3) reads 'the week of the year, ((week mod 52) + 52) mod 52 + 1 (the non-negative remainder, so a replay week before creation reads its season)'.

issues.claim: The replay's stream key differs between §4.11 and §6.1. §4.11 *History-first generation* (2) (l. 7671) says the replay's epochs 'draw on the ordinary …/epoch=e streams (§6.1)'. §6.1's epoch component (l. 8621-8623; J-A113.61) keys the replay's coarse epochs r = 1 … R with 0x8000 + r, 'so no replay draw can equal a live epoch's'. Read literally, §4.11 has replay epoch r draw live epoch r's numbers, which correlates the replayed past with the town's first live epochs. Determinism's cross-part note asks §4.11 to use the replay epoch component.
issues.required_change: §4.11 *History-first generation* (2) reads '... they draw on the epoch streams keyed with the replay's epoch component 0x8000 + r (§6.1; J-A113.61), so the replay is deterministic from the seed and the history and no replay draw equals a live epoch's; ...'.

issues.claim: The bent-cut ladder's six-call bound is lost. The archived §5.2 F-CUT row (archive l. 6894) said 'on 10⁵ random concave and holed faces the ladder ends in ≤ 6 kernel calls and the face count never decreases'. Neither number now appears anywhere in the base. §5.2 also cites '§4.6 step 8 (a)'s area bound', but the area bound is in rung (d).

Determinism's §5.2 F-CUT row then cites '§4.6 step 8's acceptance' and '§4.6 step 8 (d)'s area bound' in place of '§4.6 step 8 (a)'s bars' and '§4.6 step 8 (a)'s area bound'.

issues.claim: The water pull ignores a spring's flow. §4.2 S3 (6) (l. 4928-4931) defines q(x) as 1 at 'a lake or oasis shore, a spring or ground of the top well-yield class', falling to 0 at the pull radius, and §4.5's water term (l. 5550-5552) reads the same q. Neither reads WaterBody.spring.flow (§2.3, l. 926, a share of full flow in (0, 1]). V06 §3.12.1 (l. 1980-1982) says 'its flow ... weights its water pull on the growth field (§4.2 S3 (6), §4.4) and the prosperity field's water term (§4.5)', and the model's J-RM7 says §4.4 and §4.5 weight the pull by spring.flow. The base formula has no such factor. A failing spring (item 111 (b)) therefore changes no pull, and the base sentence 'a spring or oasis that fails weakens its pull' (l. 5552, 7911) has no mechanism behind it.
issues.required_change: §4.2 S3 (6)'s q(x) reads '... 1 on a river bank, a lake shore or ground of the top well-yield class; at a spring-fed water body (an oasis, WaterBody.spring) its shore and spring point give q = spring.flow (§2.3; 1 when made, lowered by V06 §3.12.1), falling linearly to 0 at the climate row's pull radius'. §4.5's water term says it reads that q, flow included.
